samples.summary: The nesting-cap predicate is duplicated byte-for-byte across backend and frontend although this same diff creates a shared home for it in `@wafflebase/docs`.
samples.evidence: `hasDocsTableAtNestingCap` (packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:231-245) and `hasTableAtNestingCap` (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:454-465) are the same recursive walk with the same `depth >= MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH` rule, and `documentHasTableAtNestingCap` (docs-tree.ts:250) duplicates the header/body/footer fan-out that `writeFullDocument` inlines in the frontend store. This diff introduces `packages/docs/src/model/table-nesting.ts` and exports it from both `src/index.ts` and `src/node.ts` — a module both packages already import (backend `docs-tree.ts` imports `MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH` from `@wafflebase/docs`; the frontend store does too) — but only the constant was shared, not the predicate the constant exists to enforce. This is the single invariant that decides whether a whole-tree write is refused on either side; two copies means a later fix (e.g. handling a table block whose `tableData` is present but rows are absent, or moving the boundary) lands in one and not the other, so the backend PUT/copy path and the editor write path can give two different answers to "does this document reach the cap?" while the design doc (docs-nested-tables.md:309) promises they behave identically.

samples.summary: The canonical tables umbrella doc still states nested tables are "recursive at any depth", which the new hard ceiling contradicts.
samples.evidence: `docs/design/docs/docs-tables.md:266` — "| `table` | **Yes** — recursive at any depth (see tables/docs-nested-tables.md) |". The change makes nesting bounded at 32 everywhere (readers truncate, producers refuse), and it correctly amended `docs-nested-tables.md` Goals, but the umbrella doc that a reader hits first still records the pre-change claim. Repo discipline is to fold into the canonical subsystem doc; here two design docs now disagree about the same invariant.

samples.summary: Large unrelated hardening subsystem (the 32-level nesting cap across importer, clipboard, model, layout, store, backend controller and copy service) is bundled into the #1049 selection fix, whose task plan scopes only two code changes.
samples.evidence: The originating task, `docs/tasks/active/20260914-table-drag-merge-selection-todo.md`, states the Plan as (1) resolve the table through `resolveNestedTableLayout()` in `selection.ts`, (2) shift+click builds an expanded `tableCellRange` in `text-editor.ts`, (3) tests — and an explicit "Out of scope" section. The diff additionally introduces `MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH` and enforcement in nine more modules across three packages, changes a public REST contract (`docs-content.controller.ts` now 400s at depth 32 rather than 33), adds a new 400 to `DocumentCopyService`, adds a silent-decline path to four incremental store writers, clamps peer-written `tableCellRange` indices, adds `blockParentMap` cycle guards in five walks, and adds a merge-expansion budget. Each may be defensible hardening, but as one change it commits the repo to a new cross-package invariant and two new user-visible API rejections under the banner of a selection-highlight bug, which makes the fix hard to review or revert independently.

samples.summary: `MAX_MERGE_EXPANSION_CELLS` introduces a caller-dependent correctness contract (exact for write paths, bounded only for the painter) that is recorded only in code comments, not in any design doc.
samples.evidence: `expandCellRangeForMerges`/`getNormalizedRange` now take a `budgetCells` parameter whose misuse is described in-code as producing "a merge that slices through an existing one — or a merged cell left uncleared", i.e. replicated corruption. That is an architectural rule binding every present and future caller of a shared helper, but `docs/design/docs/tables/docs-table-copy-paste.md:33` (the doc that documents `expandCellRangeForMerges`) and `docs/design/docs/docs-tables.md` are untouched, and `docs-nested-tables.md`'s new section covers only the nesting ceiling. Only `docs/tasks/active/20260914-table-drag-merge-selection-lessons.md:47` mentions it, and a lessons file is not a design doc under CONTRIBUTING's workflow.

samples.summary: The REST design doc's `PUT /content` validation contract is not updated for the new docs block-nesting bound, and `document-copy.md` is not updated for the new copy 400.
samples.evidence: `docs/design/rest-api.md:356-455` enumerates the `PUT` validation contract and documents only `MAX_ELEMENT_DEPTH` (the slides element walk). The docs block walk in `docs-content.controller.ts:439-458` now rejects on the *shared* `MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH` with `>=` instead of `>`, so a body that previously validated at one level now 400s — an observable API contract change absent from the API doc. Likewise `docs/design/document-copy.md` still lists the copy failure modes without the new `BadRequestException('Cannot copy this document: …')` added in `document-copy.service.ts`. Both behaviours are described in `docs-nested-tables.md`, so this is a discoverability/canonicality gap rather than an undocumented feature.

The new doc comment explains why both exist, but a reader of paste code now has to hold two unrelated numbers named almost identically; neither the clipboard nor the nested-tables design doc mentions the 8.

samples.summary: §2.5 "Nested Table Handling" still describes unbounded `convertTable` recursion; the importer now silently drops a `<w:tbl>` past the cap.
samples.evidence: `docs/design/docs/docs-docx-import-export.md:342-354` says `convertTable` recurses on the inner `<w:tbl>` and the table is appended to the parent cell, with no mention of the new drop at `MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH` added in `packages/docs/src/import/docx-importer.ts`. verdict.reason: Verified in the tree. packages/docs/src/model/table-nesting.ts exports only MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH (line 26), re-exported at index.ts:97 and node.ts:145. The nesting-cap predicate is nonetheless implemented twice with identical bodies: hasDocsTableAtNestingCap (backend docs-tree.ts:231-245) and hasTableAtNestingCap (frontend yorkie-doc-store.ts:454-465) — same skip-non-table, same `depth >= MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH` boundary, same recursion into row.cells[].blocks at depth+1. The apparent type difference is cosmetic: yorkie.types.ts:15-25 re-exports `Block as DocsBlock` from @wafflebase/docs, so both operate on the same type. The header/body/footer fan-out is duplicated too: documentHasTableAtNestingCap (docs-tree.ts:250-256) vs the inlined three-way check in writeFullDocument (yorkie-doc-store.ts:3524-3530). Reuse was available, not theoretical — docs-tree.ts:35-41 already imports MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH and docsTreeToDocument from @wafflebase/docs, and that file's own header (lines 19-23) records that the read half was de-duplicated for precisely this reason. Both copies are live: writeDocsRoot:376 and writeFullDocument:3525 gate real write paths, so neither is unreachable. The design doc states the invariant as one rule spanning both (docs/design/docs/tables/docs-nested-tables.md:309-314). Under this lens's rubric this is duplicated logic that will diverge and give two answers to the same question ("does this document reach the cap?") across the backend PUT/copy path and the editor write path — major. No refutation ground holds: not-present fails (code is as described), already-guarded fails (no guard makes either copy unreachable), out-of-scope fails (duplication/reuse is explicitly this lens's lane).
